project: Dashboard Regression Fixture and Trust Quick Wins
description: Establish a deterministic dashboard regression fixture and use it to remove duplicated outcomes-chart treatment, keep Submit Work feedback full-width and scoped to the exact Factory Session, reconcile session lists without a phantom ~default tab, and separate truthful Open Factory and New Factory journeys. This foundation lane makes basic operator workflows trustworthy and gives later dashboard work a stable behavioral baseline without absorbing the broader dashboard program.

context.customerAsk: Implement Story 0 plus the chart deduplication, submit-width/session-scoping, session-list reconciliation, and Open/New Factory quick wins from the dashboard UX probe plan. Prove every changed behavior with component and integration tests against the deterministic fixture, make the phantom ~default session impossible in that scenario, keep the Factory Sessions transport edit minimal, follow the parallel-lane rebase protocol, and deliver through actual merge.
context.problem: The dashboard's happy-path fixtures do not reproduce alias-plus-UUID identity, stale list responses, chart remounts, two-session submission races, or misleading Open/New actions. Operators can therefore see a phantom ~default tab, stale or duplicated presentation, clipped feedback, cross-session drafts/results, or validation that appears to have opened or created a Factory, despite the underlying runtime remaining correct.
context.solution: Create one CI-safe identity-keyed fixture that deterministically drives the existing typed dashboard boundaries through the assigned races and async states. Use it to prove a single chart presentation, session-scoped full-width submission feedback, authoritative canonical session-list reconciliation, and distinct non-mutating-validation/explicit-confirmation Open and New Factory flows. Keep Factory Sessions as canonical identity owner, query/session state in existing typed UI owners, and chart/tab rendering as disposable projections.

acceptanceCriteria: One deterministic, identity-keyed, CI-safe fixture reproduces alias-plus-UUID discovery, stale list refreshes, chart remount/resize, two-session submission races, and Open/New success and failure outcomes without sleeps as its primary synchronization mechanism or production-only test seams.

The fixture scenario renders each real Factory Session exactly once by canonical ID; ~default remains a selector and never appears as a second session, and successful list refreshes remove or remap stale rows and selection deterministically.

Each outcomes widget renders one chart presentation with one Y-axis title/grid treatment through loading, empty, error, success, resize, and remount behavior, with an accessible non-color-only description of the displayed values.

Submit Work drafts, pending mutations, and results never cross canonical Factory Session boundaries; feedback uses the available card width and every completion path has one localized, programmatically associated success or error state.

Open Factory and New Factory are distinct actions: validation is non-mutating, Open targets an existing Factory, New previews the exact target before confirmation, and cancel/failure cannot claim that a Factory started or was created.

Quality gate: Typecheck, focused Go/UI tests, direct browser verification, and relevant CI frontend jobs pass; there are no NEW lint violations relative to current main, and the gates green on main (backend-size, pkg-maint, pkg-file-count, pkg-structure, vet) stay green.

Delivery continues through the implementation/review loop until required CI is terminal and passing, all blocking PR conversation feedback is explicitly addressed, merge conflicts and shared-file changes are resolved under the contention protocol, and the PR is actually merged.

userStories.title: Establish the deterministic dashboard regression fixture
userStories.description: As a dashboard maintainer, I want one repeatable fixture for the assigned trust failures so every quick win and later compatible dashboard lane can prove behavior against the same canonical identities and races.
acceptanceCriteria: The fixture represents at least two canonical Factory Sessions; a ~default selector resolving to one session UUID; initial, stale, and refreshed session lists; chart loading/empty/error/success data; session-specific submit drafts and delayed outcomes; and Open/New validation, cancel, success, and failure outcomes.
Fixture records and expected rows use immutable session and result identities rather than display labels, array position, wall-clock timing, or incidental rendered text as identity.

Component and browser scenarios can advance list refreshes, session changes, mutation completions, and chart states by deterministic controls or observable promises; sleeps and timeout padding are not the primary synchronization mechanism.

The fixture reuses existing typed API, query, session-store, and component boundaries and adds no production-only test hook, second event/replay implementation, live network dependency, or filesystem topology assertion.
The focused fixture scenario is stable in repeated local runs and CI and provides the shared setup used by Stories 002–005.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify the fixture-driven dashboard scenario in a real browser at one mobile viewport and one desktop viewport
userStories.notes: Implemented the shared deterministic dashboard regression fixture and controller under ui/src/components/dashboard/fixtures, covering canonical Factory Session identity, ~default resolution, stale/refreshed out-of-order lists, chart states and remount widths, session-scoped delayed submissions, and Open/New outcomes. Added typed API/session-provider component coverage, a Storybook interaction scenario, and mobile/desktop browser viewport coverage. Verified with TypeScript, Bun unit tests, the focused Vitest component test, biome/lint and test-lane guards, Storybook build, the focused Canonical Storybook interaction filter, and the dashboard viewport browser check. Stories 002–005 remain intentionally open for later iterations.

userStories.title: Render one outcomes chart treatment
userStories.description: As an operator, I want each outcomes widget to show one coherent visualization so duplicated chart or axis treatment cannot make the displayed results look inflated or broken.
acceptanceCriteria: For every Story 0 chart state, one outcomes widget renders exactly one chart visualization, one Y-axis title, and one grid/axis treatment; refresh, remount, responsive resize, and Strict Mode-style rerendering do not duplicate them.

Loading shows an explicit loading state, known-empty data shows an explicit empty state without a misleading plot, failures show an actionable localized error state, and valid data shows the single chart.
The visible chart values have an accessible textual description or data view, and series are distinguishable without relying on color alone.
The chart remains contained by and fills the available widget width at the Story 0 mobile and desktop viewports without horizontal page overflow.
Focused component and integration regressions use the Story 0 fixture and fail if a second chart, Y-axis title, or grid treatment appears.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify the chart directly in a real browser at mobile and desktop widths, including a resize or remount transition
userStories.notes: Removed the duplicate CartesianGrid and duplicate Recharts Y-axis title, keeping one dashed grid treatment and one overlay-owned Y-axis title. Added a localized aria-describedby data description that follows visible series, preserving dashed line patterns and legend labels for non-color distinction. Added Story 0 fixture-backed Strict Mode/remount/state component coverage, localized message coverage, Storybook one-treatment assertions, and the Playwright Storybook browser gate at 320px and 1280px with a live resize. TypeScript, UI lint, focused Bun/Vitest component tests, Storybook build, and the direct browser gate pass. The exact WorkChart Storybook file still reports its pre-existing Constrained Width legend-height ratio failure (5/6 stories pass); the new direct browser check passes that story at both viewports, so the unrelated harness assertion is recorded rather than changing sizing policy.

userStories.title: Keep Submit Work full-width and session-scoped
userStories.description: As an operator working across Factory Sessions, I want my draft and submission result to stay with the exact destination and use the available card width so I cannot accidentally submit to or annotate another session.
acceptanceCriteria: Draft values, validation, pending state, and completion feedback are keyed to the exact canonical Factory Session selected when the operation is composed or submitted; switching from fixture session A to B never copies A's draft into B or submits A's content to B.
A late success or failure from session A cannot replace, annotate, or announce session B's composer state, and returning to A shows only the state intentionally retained for A.
Every submit path exposes the visible canonical destination before confirmation and renders exactly one localized, programmatically associated loading, success, or error state for its owning session.
The submission status/receipt region uses the full available widget width, wraps long localized content, and introduces no horizontal page overflow at the Story 0 mobile and desktop viewports.
Controls, labels, validation messages, and focus behavior remain semantic and keyboard operable during validation, submission, session switching, success, and retryable failure.
Focused component and integration regressions use the Story 0 two-session delayed-completion scenario.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify the A-to-B draft and late-completion journey directly in a real browser at mobile and desktop widths
userStories.notes: Keyed rich and simple Submit Work drafts, pending states, receipts, file staging, and late completion guards by the exact canonical Factory Session ID. Added visible canonical destinations, localized programmatic success/error/loading associations, full-width wrapping feedback, and an explicit accessible form name. Added fixture-backed A-to-B delayed success/failure component regressions, a passive Storybook fixture harness with deterministic completion controls, and a Playwright browser gate at 390px and 1440px that checks draft isolation, late-result isolation, canonical destinations, full-width feedback, and page overflow. TypeScript, focused Biome/lint and boundary checks, focused Vitest composer/status tests, the native Bun SubmitWorkCard suite, Storybook build, Storybook CI scheduling test, and the direct mobile/desktop browser gate pass. Stories 004 and 005 remain intentionally open for later iterations.

userStories.title: Reconcile Factory Session lists to canonical identity
userStories.description: As an operator, I want refreshed Factory Session tabs to represent the backend's current canonical sessions exactly once so aliases and stale responses cannot create phantom or obsolete choices.
acceptanceCriteria: When live and durable listing inputs refer to the same canonical session, the Factory Sessions listing boundary returns one canonical row with the resolved session ID; ~default is accepted only as a selector and is not returned or rendered as an additional durable session identity.

After a successful fixture refresh, the latest authoritative session list replaces stale membership: removed sessions disappear, newly available sessions appear once, and the selected alias or obsolete row remaps to its resolved canonical session or an explicit no-session state.
A slower response for an older list request cannot overwrite a newer successful reconciliation or recreate a removed or phantom tab.

Initial loading, no-session, retained-data refresh, refresh failure, and successful reconciliation have explicit UI treatment; a failure does not silently present retained rows as freshly confirmed and exposes a keyboard-operable retry.
Tabs use truthful navigation or tab/panel semantics, stable unique accessible names, visible focus, keyboard ordering, and responsive overflow without pointing controls at an empty panel.
Focused Go transport tests and UI component/integration tests use the Story 0 alias-plus-UUID and out-of-order refresh scenarios and prove that no ~default phantom session is reproducible.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify canonical tab rendering, stale-row removal, retry, and keyboard navigation directly in a real browser at mobile and desktop widths
userStories.notes: Reconciled Factory Session list identity at the Go mapping boundary and the typed UI API boundary: selector-only ~default rows are removed, duplicate rows collapse by canonical ID, and canonical UUID summaries remain authoritative. Added store reconciliation for membership, tab order, paused state, selected-session fallback, and resolved default selection; refresh requests use query cancellation signals and retained-data failures render a localized retry state without hiding existing tabs. Extended the deterministic fixture/controller, component regressions, canonical Storybook story, and mobile/desktop Playwright gate with stale-row removal, keyboard Home/End ordering, refresh failure/retry, responsive overflow, and alias-plus-UUID coverage. Verified with TypeScript, focused Bun unit/component suites, focused Go mapping/HTTP suites, UI lint and boundary/test-lane guards, rebuilt Storybook, focused Storybook interaction (canonical story passed; 2 unrelated stories skipped), direct browser verification at 390x844 and 1440x900, and git diff --check. Story 005 remains intentionally open for the next iteration.

userStories.title: Separate Open Factory and New Factory journeys
userStories.description: As an operator, I want distinct Open and New Factory actions so I know whether I am selecting an existing Factory or creating a new target before anything starts.
acceptanceCriteria: Open Factory and New Factory are separately named, discoverable actions with distinct dialogs or modes; Open selects an existing target, while New collects and previews the exact normalized target that will be created.
Validation and preview are non-mutating and never report that a Factory was opened, created, or started; only explicit final confirmation invokes the matching operation once.

Cancel, dialog dismissal, validation failure, missing or broken Open target, and create failure leave session membership unchanged, restore focus to the invoking control, and show no false success state.

Each journey exposes explicit loading, empty, error, and success treatment where applicable, with localized copy, semantic labels and errors, visible focus, complete keyboard operation, and non-color-only status.
Successful Open or New completion invalidates and reconciles the canonical session list from Story 004, selects the resulting canonical session once, and does not add a ~default tab.
Dialogs and action controls remain usable without page overflow at the Story 0 mobile and desktop viewports.
Focused component and integration regressions use the Story 0 Open/New outcomes and canonical session-list reconciliation.
Typecheck passes
Tests pass
Verify Open, New preview and confirmation, cancel and focus restoration, and a failure path directly in a real browser at mobile and desktop widths
